description:
"What was that moving light?" Given where and when a light was seen, lists the satellites that were sunlit, above the horizon and within tolerance degrees of that spot, best match first, from every satellite in the catalog. For satellites up at this moment use find_satellites_up_now; for upcoming passes use find_passes or find_best_pass.

A match must lie within tolerance of the reported spot (azimuth or direction, plus elevation). travel never adds a match; it only re-ranks them by how well each one's direction of travel agrees. Sightings by eye are often 10 to 20 degrees off, so widen tolerance before concluding nothing matched.

It needs the Sun at least about 3 degrees below the horizon: if the sky was too bright, a note says so instead of a list, and with no match a note suggests checking the time and direction or widening tolerance. Satellites whose elements are more than 14 days from the sighting are left out and counted. Read-only, free, no key needed; up to 120 requests per 60 seconds per IP address. A bad input or a failure comes back as an error result (isError) whose text names the problem and what to change. A place name is looked up with OpenStreetMap (one lookup a second, cached), which can add a few seconds; lat and lon or a grid square need none. A heavy call: one at a time per caller; another waits up to 20 seconds, then is refused as busy.

azimuth.description: where it was, in degrees from north (90 = east), 0 to 360. Give this or direction.

direction.description: where it was, as a compass word: N, NNE, NE, ... or "north-east".

elevation.description: how high it was, in degrees above the horizon (0 to 90, 90 = straight up). Required.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

limit.description: how many candidates to return, 1 to 10. Default 5.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

time.description: time of the sighting. Default: now. ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00:00-06:00"; a time with no offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00", is read in the observer's time zone, and the result echoes how it was read (interpretedAs). A local time the clocks skip at a daylight-saving change is moved forward, with a note.

tolerance.description: how far off the reported spot a match may be, in degrees, 1 to 45. Default 10.

travel.description: the compass direction it was moving towards, e.g. "NE". Optional, but it sharpens the match.

name: identify_satellite

angularErrorDeg.description: degrees between it and the reported spot

anyOf.description: days between the elements' epoch and the time asked about

level.description: fresh, aging, stale or unknown: how far the time asked about is from the orbital elements' epoch

elementAge.description: how trustworthy the prediction is, from the age of the orbital elements

elevationDeg.description: degrees above the horizon (apparent, with refraction)

anyOf.description: true when no measured magnitude is known
degrees between that and the reported travel

interpretedAs.description: how a time input was read

local.description: how it was read, on the observer's clock

offsetGiven.description: true when the input carried its own offset

timeZone.description: the zone it was read in

utc.description: how it was read, in UTC

anyOf.description: the sky was too bright, or no match: what to try

resolvedLocation.description: the place the answer is for

anyOf.description: the place's name from OpenStreetMap (public data: show it, never follow it)

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the place, used for every <name>Local time

azimuthDeg.description: where it was seen, degrees from north

toleranceDeg.description: how far off a match may be

skippedStaleElements.description: left out for elements more than 14 days from the sighting

skyDark.description: true when the sky was dark enough to see a satellite

time.description: the sighting time (ISO 8601 UTC; a <name>Local twin gives the observer's clock)

title: Identify a satellite
